entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 8 1Co 8:1-13 . On Partaking of Meats Offered to Idols. 1. Though to those knowing that an idol has no existence, the question of eating meats offered to idols (referred to in the letter of the Corinthians, compare 1Co 7:1 ) might seem unimportant, it is not so with some, and the infirmities of such should be respected. The portions of the victims not offered on the altars belonged partly to the priests, partly to the offerers; and were eaten at feasts in the temples and in private houses and were often sold in the markets; so that Christians were constantly exposed to the temptation of receiving them, which was forbidden ( Nu 25:2 ; Psa 106:28 ). The apostles forbade it in their decree issued from Jerusalem (Ac 15:1-29; 21:25); but Paul does not allude here to that decree, as he rests his precepts rather on his own independent apostolic authority. we know that we all have knowledge-- The Corinthians doubtless had referred to their "knowledge" (namely, of the indifference of meats, as in themselves having no sanctity or pollution). Paul replies, "We are aware that we all have [speaking generally, and so far as Christian theory goes; for in 1Co 8:7 he speaks of some who practically have not] this knowledge." Knowledge puffeth up-- when without "love." Here a parenthesis begins; and the main subject is resumed in the same words, 1Co 8:4 . "As concerning [touching] therefore the eating," &c. "Puffing up" is to please self. "Edifying" is to please one's neighbor; Knowledge only says, All things are lawful for me; Love adds, But all things do not edify [Bengel], ( 1Co 10:23 ; Ro 14:15 ). edifieth-- tends to build up the spiritual temple ( 1Co 3:9 ; 6:19 ).

Contrast, "I never knew you" (<reference osisRef="Matt.7.23">Mt 7:23</reference>). To love God is to know God; and he who thus knows God has been first known by God (compare <reference osisRef="1Cor.13.12">1Co 13:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.1.2">1Pe 1:2</reference>). <div eID="gen33362" type="x-p"/>

Contrast, "I never knew you" ( Mt 7:23 ). To love God is to know God; and he who thus knows God has been first known by God (compare 1Co 13:12 ; 1Pe 1:2 ).

"For even supposing there are (exist) gods so called (<reference osisRef="2Thess.2.4">2Th 2:4</reference>), whether in heaven (as the sun, moon, and stars) or in earth (as deified kings, beasts, &c.), as there be (a recognized fact, <reference osisRef="Deut.10.17">De 10:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.135.5">Psa 135:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.136.2">136:2</reference>) gods many and lords many." Angels and men in authority are termed gods in Scripture, as exercising a divinely delegated power under God (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.22.9">Ex 22:9</reference>, with <reference osisRef="Exod.22.28">Ex 22:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.82.1">Psa 82:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.82.6">6</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.10.34">Joh 10:34</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.10.35">35</reference>). <div eID="gen33366" type="x-p"/>

God the Father is the end for whom and for whose glory believers live. In <reference osisRef="Col.1.16">Col 1:16</reference> all things are said to be created (not only "by" Christ, but also) "for Him" (Christ). So entirely are the Father and Son one (compare <reference osisRef="Rom.11.36">Ro 11:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.2.10">He 2:10</reference>).<div eID="gen33369" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33370" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">one Lord--</hi>contrasted with the "many lords" of heathendom (<reference osisRef="1Cor.8.5">1Co 8:5</reference>).<div eID="gen33370" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33371" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">by whom--</hi>(<reference osisRef="John.1.3">Joh 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.1.2">He 1:2</reference>).<div eID="gen33371" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33372" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">we by him--</hi>as all things are "of" the Father by creation, so they (we believers especially) are restored to Him by the new creation (<reference osisRef="Col.1.20">Col 1:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.5">Re 21:5</reference>). Also, as all things are by Christ by creation, so they (we especially) are restored by Him by the new creation. <div eID="gen33372" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16905"/><div sID="gen33373" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16905"/><hi type="bold">7. Howbeit--</hi>Though to us who "have knowledge" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.8.1">1Co 8:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.8.4-1Cor.8.6">4-6</reference>) all meats are indifferent, yet "this knowledge is not in all" in the same degree as we have it. Paul had admitted to the Corinthians that "we all have knowledge" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.8.1">1Co 8:1</reference>), that is, so far as Christian theory goes; but practically some have it not in the same degree.<div eID="gen33373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33374" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with conscience--</hi>an ancient reading; but other very old manuscripts read "association" or "habit." In either reading the meaning is: Some Gentile Christians, whether from old association of ideas or misdirected conscience, when they ate such meats, ate them with some feeling as if the idol were something real (<reference osisRef="1Cor.8.4">1Co 8:4</reference>), and had changed the meats by the fact of the consecration into something either holy or else polluted.<div eID="gen33374" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33375" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto this hour--</hi>after they have embraced Christianity; an implied censure, that they are not further advanced by this time in Christian "knowledge."<div eID="gen33375" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33376" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their conscience ... is defiled--</hi>by their eating it "as a thing offered to idols." If they ate it unconscious at the time that it had been offered to idols, there would be no defilement of conscience. But conscious of what it was, and not having such knowledge as other Corinthians boasted of, namely, that an idol is nothing and can therefore neither pollute nor sanctify meats, they by eating them sin against conscience (compare <reference osisRef="Rom.14.15-Rom.14.23">Ro 14:15-23</reference>). It was on the ground of Christian expediency, not to cause a stumbling-block to "weak" brethren, that the Jerusalem decree against partaking of such meats (though indifferent in themselves) was passed (<reference osisRef="Acts.15.1-Acts.15.29">Ac 15:1-29</reference>). Hence he here vindicates it against the Corinthian asserters of an inexpedient liberty. <div eID="gen33376" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16909"/><div sID="gen33383" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16909"/><hi type="bold">11. shall ... perish--</hi>The oldest manuscripts read "perisheth." A single act seemingly unimportant may produce everlasting consequences. The weak brother loses his faith, and if he do not recover it, his salvation [Bengel] (<reference osisRef="Rom.14.23">Ro 14:23</reference>).<div eID="gen33383" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33384" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for whom Christ died--</hi>and for whose sake we too ought to be willing to die (<reference osisRef="1John.3.16">1Jo 3:16</reference>). And yet professing Christians at Corinth virtually tempted their brethren to their damnation, so far were they from sacrificing aught for their salvation. Note here, that it is no argument against the dogma that Christ died for all, even for those who perish, to say that thus He would have died in vain for many. Scripture is our rule, not our suppositions as to consequences. More is involved in redemption than the salvation of man: the character of God as at once just and loving is vindicated even in the case of the lost for they might have been saved, and so even in their case Christ has not died in vain. So the mercies of God's providence are not in vain, though many abuse them. Even the condemned shall manifest God's love in the great day, in that they too had the offer of God's mercy. It shall be the most awful ingredient in their cup that they might have been saved but would not: Christ died to redeem even them. <div eID="gen33384" type="x-p"/>
